title: Local Prefetch Proxy (LPP) PRD: predictive prefetching and local caching for hybrid deployments
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This Product Requirements Document describes the Local Prefetch Proxy (LPP): a lightweight agent and proxy layer that runs alongside Redwood Private and Dedicated edge gateways to reduce end-to-end latency, egress, and per-token cost by proactively prefetching model prefixes, embeddings, and small-model results. LPP aims to preserve model fidelity while improving observable economics for customers that operate in hybrid or private modes.

Why this exists (motivation)

- Customers operating private or dedicated deployments see disproportionate egress and cold-start costs for common short sequences (chat greetings, system prompts, knowledge snippets) and re-used embedding lookups.
- Many workloads exhibit high temporal locality (repeated prompts, similar session prefixes, retrieval pipelines) that can be leveraged to prefetch or cache safely.
- Current caching mechanisms are either coarse (full-response caches) or rely on application-layer change; platform-level prefetching enables consistent, low-effort wins for customers.

Background and constraints

- LPP is targeted for Redwood Private (VPC & on-prem) and Dedicated deployments; hosted API customers will get a managed variant later.
- Must respect confidentiality and data-residency: no cross-tenant sharing of cached artifacts.
- Prefetch decisions must be cost-aware and reversible (easy to disable per-route).

Goals (measurable)

1. Reduce mean tail latency (95th percentile) for common chat routes by >= 20% in first-line enterprise workloads.
2. Reduce per-request token cost for qualifying routes by >= 12% through reduced repeated computation (prefix reuse + small-model caching) within first 6 months of adoption.
3. Provide per-route visibility and toggle controls in Console with >= 99% accuracy in reported cache hits/misses.
4. Rollout to GA for Dedicated and Private with a documented security review and migration playbook.

Non-goals

- LPP will not replace long-term semantic knowledge stores or vector DBs.
- LPP is not a universal full-response CDN; it focuses on prefix/kv/embedding/small-model artifacts.

User stories

- Platform engineer: "As a platform engineer, I want to enable LPP per-service with a conservative prefetch policy so that critical chat flows get consistent latency without changing application code."
- Product manager: "As a PM, I want to see the cost delta per route after enabling LPP to decide packaging."
- DevOps: "As a DevOps lead, I need an emergency off switch for LPP and audit logs to prove regulatory compliance."

Functional requirements

1. Agent and Proxy
   - LPP consists of (A) a local agent running on the host (container/VM) that collects lightweight telemetry and (B) an HTTP proxy layer that intercepts Redwood inference calls and consults the local cache and prefetch policy.
   - Deployable as sidecar (Kubernetes) and systemd-managed daemon (on-prem bare metal).

2. Prefetch heuristics and modes
   - Heuristics: frequency-based (most-common prefixes), session-based (predict next token ranges), retrieval-triggered (when embedding keys are read), and ML-backed predictor (optional advanced mode).
   - Modes: off | observe-only | conservative-prefetch | aggressive-prefetch | predictive (ML).

3. Artifacts to cache/prefetch
   - Static system prompts (sha256-keyed), small-model outputs (classification/NER results under 2KB), embedding vectors (with TTL policies), and KV-cache prefixes for decoder models (by lineage-safe keys).

4. API surface and Console controls
   - Per-route enable/disable toggle, mode selector, budget (tokens-per-minute), and max cache size per tenant.
   - Console must show: cache hit rate, hit savings (token/cost), and recent prefetch trace.

5. Security and data governance
   - Cache keys and artifacts stored encrypted (customer KMS when available).
   - Cache must honor data-residency and not replicate artifacts outside configured regions.
   - Audit events for prefetch actions and cache evictions retained for 90 days.

6. Billing attribution and cost controls
   - Prefetch actions must be attributed to a route/client API key for billing and accounting.
   - Administrative quotas to cap prefetch token spend per tenant/route.

Non-functional requirements

- Startup: agent must boot within 2s and not add >2ms median overhead when set to observe-only.
- Resource footprint: default memory <= 256MB, disk <= 2GB (configurable).
- Reliability: cache lookups should not increase error rate; fallback to platform when local errors occur.
- Observability: emit metrics via Prometheus-compatible endpoint and structured logs via JSON.

Acceptance criteria (high level)

1. End-to-end test harness demonstrates >= 20% 95p latency reduction on 3 representative customer workloads with conservative-prefetch on.
2. Console shows correct attribution for prefetch cost within +/- 5% of raw billing data across 7-day window.
3. Security review signed and all encryption/permissions behaviors pass internal compliance checklist.

API / Proxy contract (examples)

- Example request flow when LPP is enabled (sidecar proxy intercept):
  1) Client -> LPP proxy: POST /v1/generate {"route": "chat-service-prod", "input": "Hello"} 
  2) Proxy checks cache for matching prefix/kv. On hit: return cached continuation token or short response. On miss: forward to Redwood runtime, record candidate artifacts for prefetching.

- Example JSON header flags (client->proxy):
  {
    "X-Redwood-Route": "chat-service-prod",
    "X-LPP-Mode": "conservative",
    "X-LPP-Budget": "5000"
  }

Configuration example (YAML)

- lpp-config.yaml (per-tenant; simplified):
  tenant_id: tenant-acme
  enabled_routes:
    - name: chat-service-prod
      mode: conservative-prefetch
      token_budget_per_minute: 6000
      max_cache_mb: 512
  global_defaults:
    observe_only_ttl_secs: 300
    default_mode: observe-only

Observability and metrics (key metric names)

- lpp.cache.hits_total (counter)
- lpp.cache.misses_total (counter)
- lpp.prefetch.requests_total (counter)
- lpp.prefetch.tokens_spent (counter)
- lpp.latency.added_ms (histogram)
- lpp.saved_tokens_estimate (gauge)
- lpp.audit.prefetch_event (structured log stream)

SLOs for LPP behavior (platform-provided)

- Cache lookup success latency: P99 <= 10ms (local disk) or <= 20ms (NFS).
- Prefetch failure ratio <= 0.5% (prefetch attempts leading to proxy errors).
- Console reporting freshness <= 60s for key metrics.

Security and compliance notes

- All cached artifacts are stored encrypted with AES-256; customers with KMS configured will have keys stored by their KMS.
- LPP will expose an enforcement boundary to redact or opt-out of caching for specified data labels (PII), integrated with the Redwood data-classification library.

Pricing and packaging implications (summary)

- Feature packaging options to consider:
  - Beta add-on: included for Dedicated with no extra charge for first 90 days.
  - Capacity-bundled: discounted prefetch token pool when purchased with Reserved Capacity (Dedicated).
  - Enterprise: per-tenant KMS support and extended audit retention as a paid add-on.

- Billing model: charge prefetch tokens at a discounted rate relative to on-demand tokens (configurable; recommended default 0.6x) and show separate line-item in billing export for transparency.

Rollout plan (phases)

1. Internal alpha (4 weeks)
   - Deploy to staging clusters, test with synthetic workloads, validate metrics.
   - Owners: eng-serving-runtime (runtime), eng-private-deployments (deploy).
2. Private beta (8–12 weeks)
   - Offer to 5 customers in Dedicated/Private as opt-in. Monitor cost impact and fidelity regressions.
   - Update Console with per-route controls and reporting.
3. GA (post-12 weeks)
   - After compliance sign-off and performance validation, enable self-serve in Console.

Rollout checklists (numbered)

1. Security review complete (sign-off by Security)
2. Telemetry schema published and dashboards created in Console
3. Billing integration: prefetch attribution verified on sandbox billing export
4. Migration doc and emergency off-switch validated

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Over-prefetching increases cost.
  Mitigation: Conservative default mode, per-route budgets, and automated spend alarms.
- Risk: Accuracy of predictive model leads to fidelity regressions.
  Mitigation: Observe-only mode for first 7 days; A/B tests with canary traffic split; automated prompt-set evaluations for quality regression detection.
- Risk: Regulatory concerns about caching PII.
  Mitigation: Data classification integration to exclude sensitive tokens; per-tenant opt-out.

Ownership and milestones

- Product lead: Aisha Patel
- Technical lead: Jared Kim (eng-serving-runtime)
- Deployment lead: Priya Desai (eng-private-deployments)
- Security reviewer: Nina Gupta

Milestones (quarterly)
- Q4 2028: Internal alpha & telemetry
- Q1 2029: Private beta with 5 customers
- Q2 2029: GA and billing integration

Appendix: Example curl flows and debugging commands

- Start sidecar (Kubernetes):
  kubectl apply -f k8s/lpp-sidecar.yaml

- Debugging: check Prometheus metrics endpoint
  curl http://localhost:9101/metrics | grep lpp.cache

- Sample trace log (JSON):
  {
    "ts":"2028-10-12T15:23:12Z",
    "tenant":"tenant-acme",
    "route":"chat-service-prod",
    "event":"prefetch",
    "artifact":"system-prompt-3b73f",
    "tokens_spent":42,
    "decision_mode":"conservative"
  }

Migration notes for existing customers

- For Dedicated customers: LPP can be toggled on per-cluster; recommend starting in observe-only mode for 2 weeks and then enabling conservative-prefetch. Provide a migration script to map existing route names to LPP configuration.
- For Private on-prem: provide offline installer and an audit checklist for security teams.

Document maintenance

- Owner to review quarterly and update SLOs and billing recommendations after the beta.
- Related implementation docs: eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/lpp-deploy.md (TBD) and eng-private-deployments/customer-installation-guide-lpp.md (TBD).
